advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard _NEVER_COUNTED_SCAN_KINDS against drift by deriving/asserting it from the per-site is_issue=False flags (a runtime or generative-test check that exercises every emitted informational kind), not just pinning it to a frozen literal.
evidence: fsck_tracker_health.py:60-62 only a NOTE comment: 'any pair added here with is_issue=False ... MUST also be reflected in fsck._NEVER_COUNTED_KINDS'

test_never_counted_kinds_is_exactly_scan_plus_dirty_components pins the set to exact literals `{"push_pending", "status_fork_resolved", "warn"}`, which cannot detect a newly-added production kind that was omitted from the literal — the drift guard is only effective for the dirty specs, which are derived, not for the scan set
advisory.finding: _NEVER_COUNTED_SCAN_KINDS is a hand-maintained literal frozenset that must be kept in lock-step with inline is_issue=False decisions at production sites (fsck_scan status_fork_resolved, _tracker_health WARN/branch-mismatch, _tracker_sync_status push_pending). A future is_issue=False scan/health kind added without updating this set silently becomes counted=True in JSON, so issue_count over-counts and again disagrees with the exit code — the exact bug being fixed. Only NOTE comments guard this seam; no runtime assertion or generative test derives it from the per-site flags (unlike the dirty specs, which are single-sourced).
scenarios: A developer adds a new tracker-level informational check with is_issue=False to _tracker_health's tuple and emits a new KIND: line, but does not add that kind to _NEVER_COUNTED_SCAN_KINDS.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider the internal-constant equality assertions in test_never_counted_kinds_is_exactly_scan_plus_dirty_components (change-detector on private structure).
evidence: Rule-4 litmus: renaming/reorganizing these private constants (a behavior-preserving refactor) breaks the assertion with no observable-behavior change; the actual invariant (counted subset == exit-code tally) is exercised by test_counted_tally_equals_exit_code_tally_for_every_never_counted_kind and test_cli_json_issue_count_agrees_with_exit_code.
advisory.finding: The drift-guard test asserts internal module constants (their names, decomposition into scan|dirty components, and the literal scan set) rather than observable behavior; it would break on a behavior-preserving refactor that renames or inlines these private constants, while the exit-code/JSON agreement it protects is already covered behaviorally by the parametrized transform tests and the CLI end-to-end test.

evidence: test_cli_json_issue_count_agrees_with_exit_code seeds only _seed_missing_create(rebar_repo) (a single counted finding) — no never-counted kind co-present in the real run.

The mixed-kind tally check test_counted_tally_equals_exit_code_tally_for_every_never_counted_kind uses _payload(...) (synthetic text lines fed to _transform_json), not a real _scan run, so it re-derives via the same transform rather than driving _scan.
Existing tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_push_pending.py:65 asserts PUSH_PENDING stays exit 0 via _cli.main(["fsck"]) text output, never --output json / issue_count.
advisory.finding: No end-to-end test drives a REAL store that simultaneously emits a report-only kind (e.g. push_pending) AND a counted finding through `--output json` to confirm issue_count excludes the report-only kind while agreeing with the exit code — the exact regression class the diff fixes. The only real-store CLI json test seeds one counted missing_create with no never-counted kind present; the mixed-kind agreement is proven only via synthetic _transform_json text lines, and existing push_pending real-store tests use text output.
